with the work undone → fails visibly, with auto-commit on fail recovery, exit **1**\\n- D11 `?? .formal-ai/` counted as user changes, re-created by every restart so the blocker never cleared → `src/ai-tool-scratch.lib.mjs` excludes AI scratch state via `.git/info/exclude`\\n\\n**Not calling nothing a success**\\n\\n- D8 `- 1 file(s) modified` for an empty net diff → measured from the diff, Problem Solving:\n\n   Root causes now proven by local reproduction (formal-ai 0.317.0, claude 2.1.220, codex-cli 0.146.0, agent 0.25.5):\n\n   - **claude + formal-ai (upstream formal-ai bug + Hive Mind exposure).** `formal-ai with <tool>` scans the passthrough arguments case-insensitively for workspace-effect intent substrings (`create`, `write`, `implement`) and, on a match, switches into an orchestration/recovery mode in which it (a) prepends its own orchestration args, (b) **consumes stdin without forwarding it**, and (c) replaces the prompt with its own recovery prompt passed as `-p The previous attempt in this session finished without changing the workspace.…Request: <the arguments>'`. Hive Mind's claude invocation always contains `--disallowedTools … CronCreate …`, so the real prompt is always discarded and claude aborts with `Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print` → exit 1, zero tokens. Verified triggers: `Write`, `CronCreate`, `create`, `CREATE`, `writes`, `implement`, `Createx`, `xCreate`, `zzcreatezz`; non-triggers: `wrote`, `modify`, `update`, `delete`, `Bash`, `Read`, `Edit`, `Monitor`, `NotebookEdit`, and any number of generic `ToolN` values. Probes show the same stdin loss for **agent, gemini, qwen and opencode** when a keyword-bearing arg is present (STDIN-BYTES 20 → 0). Verified Hive Mind fix: pass the prompt as `-p \"<prompt>\"` (exit 0, `stdin-lost: false`) — which also makes execution match the already-displayed \"Raw command\".\n\n   - **codex + formal-ai (Hive Mind bug triggered by codex arg semantics).** `formal-ai with codex` correctly injects `-c model_providers.formalai.{name,base_url,env_key,wire_api} -c model_catalog_json=… -c model_provider=\"formalai\" -c model=\"formal-ai\"` **before** the `exec` subcommand, but codex 0.146.0 lets `-c` overrides given **after** `exec` *replace* the global ones. Hive Mind passes `-c model_reasoning_effort=none -c model_context_window=… -c model_auto_compact_token_limit=[REDACTED] after `exec`, wiping the entire Formal AI provider config → codex falls back to the built-in `openai` provider (rollout `\"model_provider\":\"openai\"`), hits `wss://api.openai.com/v1/responses` → 401 (and formal-ai's server log records zero requests), plus the `Model metadata for 'formal-ai' not found` warning (the catalog override is wiped too) and the missing `-o` last-message file. Verified fix: place Hive Mind's `-c` overrides **before** `exec` → `\"model_provider\":\"formalai\"`, exit 0, last-message file written. Also learned `wire_api=\"chat\"` is rejected by codex 0.146.0 (\"no longer supported\", ref openai/codex discussion 7782) and Formal AI's `/api/openai/v1` does implement the Responses API.\n\n   - **agent + formal-ai.** The pipeline works end-to-end (correct provider, tokens, $0.00 cost, `5/5` auto-restart budget, empty-PR detection), but Formal AI only writes `.formal-ai/general-change-plan.lino` and reports \"preserved the requested goal without claiming unobserved source edits\" — no source edits, hence an empty PR. That is the upstream Formal AI capability issue. Hive Mind side: `src/agent.lib.mjs` never reads `data.part.text`, so the assistant's text is dropped and `resultSummary` is null → false-negative \"No working session summary available from AI tool output\".\n\n   Additional Hive-Mind-side defect candidates identified from the logs but not yet root-caused: `gh: Not Found (HTTP 404)` stderr noise plus raw GitHub API JSON dumped to stdout; `failed to set up git credential helper: … /home/box/.gitconfig: Device or resource busy`; PR titles carrying literal quotes (`'Implement Hello World in Scala'`); PR body claiming `- 1 file(s) modified` while the API reports 0 changed files; the misleading `❌ Codex authentication failed - 401 Unauthorized` / `💡 Please run: codex login` diagnosis; `⚠️ Could not read Codex final message file: ENOENT`; `⚠️ 📈 No Codex usage found in turn.completed events`; identical prompt re-sent for all 5 auto-restart iterations with an ever-growing log re-uploaded to a new gist each time.\n\n6. Problem Solving:\n\n   Root causes are now fully proven by local reproduction (formal-ai 0.317.0, claude 2.1.220, codex-cli 0.146.0, agent 0.25.5, gemini-cli 0.53.1):\n\n   **(A) The `formal-ai with` argv wrapper is structurally incompatible with Hive Mind.** It is designed for `formal-ai with <tool> \"<prompt>\"`. It steals `--model`/`--verbose`/etc. as its own options (so `formal-ai with agent --model formal-ai --verbose` launched an **interactive** agent session), appends the rest after its own `--print`/`-p`/`exec`, and — when any argument contains workspace-effect vocabulary (`create`, `write`, `implement`; Hive Mind's `--disallowedTools … CronCreate …` always matches) — enters orchestration mode where it consumes stdin without forwarding it and replaces the prompt with its own recovery prompt. That is why Claude aborted with \"Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print\" and exited 1 with zero tokens.\n\n   **(B) codex `-c` ordering.** Overrides after `exec` wipe the globals injected before `exec`, dropping the Formal AI provider → 401 against `api.openai.com`.\n\n   **(C) Formal AI resolves tool-call paths against the server's cwd**, so files landed outside the repository clone (empty PRs) for clients that receive absolute paths (claude, codex, qwen). Mitigated by starting `formal-ai serve` with `cwd` = the clone.\n\n   **(D) Gemini headless auth** requires `settings.json`, not `GEMINI_DEFAULT_AUTH_TYPE`.\n\n   **(E) Agent result summary** — `src/agent.lib.mjs` never reads `data.part.text`, so `resultSummary` is null and `src/solve.results.lib.mjs:1374` emits the false negative \"ℹ️  No working session summary available from AI tool output\".\n\n   **(F) Formal AI content/verification quality bugs** — for \"Create a file hello.txt containing exactly: Hello World\" it wrote the content `exactly: Hello World`, and it claimed it \"verified it with `cat hello.txt`\" when the Bash tool result was `Exit code 1 / cat: hello.txt: No such file or directory`.\n\n   The verified replacement architecture (all six tools confirmed working end-to-end locally): start `formal-ai serve --agent-mode` with cwd = clone → `HOME=<isolated> formal-ai with --global --no-start-server --base-url <url> <tool>` → translate the generated config into env (`.profile` exports / `CODEX_HOME` / `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, plus the gemini `settings.json` workaround) → run the native CLI with Hive Mind's own full argument list.\n\n6. providerMap[providerId] || providerId.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + providerId.slice(1);\n};\n\n/**\n * Issue #1250: Normalize model name and find base model for pricing lookup\n * Free models like \"kimi-k2.5-free\" should use pricing from base model \"kimi-k2.5\"\n *\n * @param {string} modelName - The model name (e.g., 'kimi-k2.5-free')\n * @returns {Object} Object with:\n *   - baseModelName: The base model name for pricing lookup\n *   - isFreeVariant: Whether this is a free variant\n */\nconst getBaseModelForPricing = modelName => {\n  // Issue #1473: Use centralized freeToBaseModelMap from models/index.mjs\n\n  // Check if there's a direct mapping\n  if (freeToBaseModelMap[modelName]) {\n    return {\n      baseModelName: freeToBaseModelMap[modelName],\n      isFreeVariant: true,\n    };\n  }\n\n  // Try removing \"-free\" suffix\n  if (modelName.endsWith('-free')) {\n    return {\n      baseModelName: modelName.replace(/-free$/, ''),\n      isFreeVariant: true,\n    };\n  }\n\n  // Not a free variant\n  return {\n    baseModelName: modelName,\n    isFreeVariant: false,\n  };\n};\n\n/**\n * Calculate pricing for agent tool usage using models.dev API\n * Issue #1250: Shows actual provider (OpenCode Zen) and calculates public pricing estimate\n * based on original provider prices (Moonshot AI, OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.)\n *\n * For free models like \"kimi-k2.5-free\", this function:\n * 1. First fetches the free model info to get the model name\n * 2. Then fetches the base model (e.g., \"kimi-k2.5\") for actual pricing\n * 3. Calculates public pricing estimate based on the base model's cost\n *\n * @param {string} modelId - The model ID used (e.g., 'opencode/grok-code')\n * @param {Object} tokenUsage - Token usage data from parseAgentTokenUsage\n * @returns {Object} Pricing information with:\n *   - provider: Always \"OpenCode Zen\" (actual provider)\n *   - originalProvider: The original model provider for pricing reference\n *   - totalCostUSD: Public pricing estimate based on original provider prices\n *   - opencodeCost: Actual billed cost from OpenCode Zen (free for most models)\n */\nexport const calculateAgentPricing = async (modelId, tokenUsage) => {\n  // Issue #2119: Formal AI requests never reach OpenCode Zen, so neither the\n  // provider label nor a models.dev price lookup applies to them.\n  if (isFormalAiModel(modelId)) return buildFormalAiPricingInfo(modelId, tokenUsage);\n\n  // Extract the model name from provider/model format\n  // e.g., 'opencode/grok-code' -> 'grok-code'\n  const modelName = modelId.includes('/') ? modelId.split('/').pop() : modelId;\n\n  // Extract provider from model ID to determine original provider for pricing\n  const providerFromModel = modelId.includes('/') ? modelId.split('/')[0] : null;\n\n  // Get original provider name for pricing reference\n  let originalProvider = getOriginalProviderName(providerFromModel);\n\n  try {\n    // Fetch model info from models.dev API\n    let modelInfo = await fetchModelInfo(modelName);\n\n    // Issue #1250: Check if model has zero pricing (free model from OpenCode Zen)\n    // If so, look up the base model for actual public pricing estimate\n    const { baseModelName, isFreeVariant } = getBaseModelForPricing(modelName);\n    let baseModelInfo = null;\n    let pricingCost = modelInfo?.cost;\n\n    if (modelInfo && modelInfo.cost && modelInfo.cost.input === 0 && modelInfo.cost.output === 0 && baseModelName !== modelName) {\n      // This is a free model with zero pricing - look up base model for public pricing\n      baseModelInfo = await fetchModelInfo(baseModelName);\n      if (baseModelInfo && baseModelInfo.cost) {\n        // Use base model pricing for public estimate\n        pricingCost = baseModelInfo.cost;\n        // Update original provider from base model if available\n        if (baseModelInfo.provider && !originalProvider) {\n          originalProvider = baseModelInfo.provider;\n        }\n      }\n    }\n\n    if (modelInfo || baseModelInfo) {\n      const effectiveModelInfo = modelInfo || baseModelInfo;\n      const cost = pricingCost || { input: 0, output: 0, cache_read: 0, cache_write: 0, reasoning: 0 };\n\n      // Calculate public pricing estimate based on original provider prices\n      // Prices are per 1M tokens, so divide by 1,000,000\n      // All priced components from models.dev: input, output, cache_read, cache_write, reasoning\n      const million = new Decimal(1_000_000);\n      const inputCost = new Decimal(tokenUsage.inputTokens)\n        .mul(cost.input || 0)\n        .div(million)\n        .toNumber();\n      const outputCost = new Decimal(tokenUsage.outputTokens)\n        .mul(cost.output || 0)\n        .div(million)\n        .toNumber();\n      const cacheReadCost = new Decimal(tokenUsage.cacheReadTokens)\n        .mul(cost.cache_read || 0)\n        .div(million)\n        .toNumber();\n      const cacheWriteCost = new Decimal(tokenUsage.cacheWriteTokens)\n        .mul(cost.cache_write || 0)\n        .div(million)\n        .toNumber();\n      const reasoningCost = new Decimal(tokenUsage.reasoningTokens)\n        .mul(cost.reasoning || 0)\n        .div(million)\n        .toNumber();\n\n      const totalCost = new Decimal(inputCost).plus(outputCost).plus(cacheReadCost).plus(cacheWriteCost).plus(reasoningCost).toNumber();\n\n      // Determine if this is a free model from OpenCode Zen or Kilo Gateway\n      // Models accessed via OpenCode Zen or Kilo Gateway are free, regardless of original provider pricing\n      // Issue #1300: Added kilo provider detection for Kilo Gateway free models\n      const isOpencodeFreeModel = providerFromModel === 'opencode' || providerFromModel === 'kilo' || isFreeVariant || modelName.toLowerCase().includes('free') || modelName.toLowerCase().includes('grok') || providerFromModel === 'moonshot' || providerFromModel === 'openai' || providerFromModel === 'anthropic';\n\n      // Use base model's provider for original provider reference if available\n      const effectiveOriginalProvider = baseModelInfo?.provider || originalProvider || effectiveModelInfo?.provider || null;\n\n      return {\n        modelId,\n        modelName: effectiveModelInfo?.name || modelName,\n        // Issue #1250: Always show OpenCode Zen as actual provider\n        provider: 'OpenCode Zen',\n        // Store original provider for reference in pricing display\n        originalProvider: effectiveOriginalProvider,\n        pricing: {\n          inputPerMillion: cost.input || 0,\n          outputPerMillion: cost.output || 0,\n          cacheReadPerMillion: cost.cache_read || 0,\n          cacheWritePerMillion: cost.cache_write || 0,\n          reasoningPerMillion: cost.reasoning || 0,\n        },\n        tokenUsage,\n        breakdown: {\n          input: inputCost,\n          output: outputCost,\n          cacheRead: cacheReadCost,\n          cacheWrite: cacheWriteCost,\n          reasoning: reasoningCost,\n        },\n        // Public pricing estimate based on original/base model prices\n        totalCostUSD: totalCost,\n        // Actual cost from OpenCode Zen (free for supported models)\n        opencodeCost: isOpencodeFreeModel ? 0 : totalCost,\n        // Keep for backward compatibility - indicates if the accessed model has zero pricing\n        isFreeModel: modelInfo?.cost?.input === 0 && modelInfo?.cost?.output === 0,\n        // New flag to indicate if OpenCode Zen provides this model for free\n        isOpencodeFreeModel,\n        // Issue #1250: Include base model info for transparency\n        baseModelName: baseModelName !== modelName ? baseModelName : null,\n      };\n    }\n    // Model not found in API, return what we have\n    return {\n      modelId,\n      modelName,\n      provider: 'OpenCode Zen',\n      originalProvider,\n      tokenUsage,\n      totalCostUSD: null,\n      opencodeCost: 0, // OpenCode Zen is free\n      isOpencodeFreeModel: true,\n      error: 'Model not found in models.dev API',\n    };\n  } catch (error) {\n    // Error fetching pricing, return with error info\n    return {\n      modelId,\n      modelName,\n      provider: 'OpenCode Zen',\n      originalProvider,\n      tokenUsage,\n      totalCostUSD: null,\n      opencodeCost: 0, // OpenCode Zen is free\n      isOpencodeFreeModel: true,\n      error: error.message,\n    };\n  }\n};\n\n// return agentModels[model] || model;\n};\n\nexport const MIN_AGENT_LIVE_INPUT_VERSION = '0.24.1';\n\nexport const getAgentCliVersion = versionOutput => {\n  return semver.clean(versionOutput) || Free disk space and retry.' : `Error uploading log file: ${uploadError.message}`;\n    await log(`  ❌ ${msg}`);\n    return false;\n  }\n}\n/**\n * Helper to attach a regular comment when it fits within limits\n */\nasync function attachRegularComment(options, logComment) {\n  const fs = (await use('fs')).promises;\n  const { targetType, targetNumber, owner, repo, $, log, logFile, errorMessage, errorDuringExecution, isUsageLimit } = options;\n\n  const targetName = targetType === 'pr' ? The error to check\n * @returns {boolean} True if the error indicates rate limiting\n */\nexport function isRateLimitError(error) {\n  const errorMessage = (error.message || error.toString()).toLowerCase();\n  // Common rate limit error patterns\n  const rateLimitPatterns = ['rate limit', 'secondary rate limit', 'exceeded.*limit', 'too many requests', 'abuse detection', 'wait a few minutes', 'http 403.*rate', 'api rate limit exceeded'];\n  return rateLimitPatterns.some(pattern => {\n    return new RegExp(pattern).test(errorMessage);\n  });\n}\n/**\n * Helper function to fetch all issues with pagination and rate limiting\n * Note: GitHub Search API has a hard limit of 1000 results total.\n * For user/org queries with >1000 issues, the fetchIssuesFromRepositories fallback should be used.\n * @param {string} baseCommand - The base gh command to execute\n * @returns {Promise<Array>} Array of issues\n */\nexport async function fetchAllIssuesWithPagination(baseCommand) {\n  // Import log and cleanErrorMessage from lib.mjs\n  const { log, cleanErrorMessage } = await import('./lib.mjs');\n  try {\n    // First, try without pagination to see if we get more than the default limit\n    await log('   📊 Fetching issues with improved limits and rate limiting...', { verbose: true });\n    // Add a 5-second delay before making the API call to respect rate limits\n    await log('   ⏰ Waiting 5 seconds before API call to respect rate limits...', { verbose: true });\n    await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, timeouts.githubApiDelay));\n    const startTime = Date.now();\n    // Use appropriate page sizes: 100 for search API (more restrictive), 1000 for regular listing\n    const commandWithoutLimit = baseCommand.replace(/--limit\\s+\\d+/, '');\n    const isSearchCommand = commandWithoutLimit.includes('gh search');\n    const maxPageSize = isSearchCommand ? 100 : 1000;\n    const improvedCommand = `${commandWithoutLimit} --limit ${maxPageSize}`;\n    await log(`   🔎 Executing: ${improvedCommand}`, { verbose: true });\n    // #1756: use execGhWithRetry so transient 5xx (e.g., 504) auto-retry\n    const { stdout } = await execGhWithRetry(improvedCommand, {\n      execOptions: { encoding: 'utf8', env: process.env },\n      label: 'gh search/list issues (paginated)',\n    });\n    const endTime = Date.now();\n    const issues = JSON.parse(stdout || '[]');\n    await log(`   ✅ Fetched ${issues.length} issues in ${Math.round((endTime - startTime) / 1000)}s`);\n    // If we got exactly the max page size, there might be more - log a warning and throw error to trigger fallback\n    if (issues.length === maxPageSize) {\n      await log(`   ⚠️  Hit the ${maxPageSize} issue limit - there may be more issues available`, { level: 'warning' });\n      if (isSearchCommand) {\n        await log('   💡 GitHub Search API is limited to 1000 results max. Triggering repository fallback for complete results.', { level: 'info' });\n        // Throw an error to trigger the fallback to fetchIssuesFromRepositories which uses GraphQL pagination\n        throw new Error(`Hit search API limit of ${maxPageSize} issues - need repository-by-repository fallback for complete results`);\n      } else if (maxPageSize >= 1000) {\n        await log(`   💡 Consider filtering by labels or date ranges for repositories with >${maxPageSize} open issues`, { level: 'info' });\n      }\n    }\n    // Add a 5-second delay after the call to be extra safe with rate limits\n    await log('   ⏰ Adding 5-second delay after API call to respect rate limits...', { verbose: true });\n    await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, timeouts.githubApiDelay));\n    return issues;\n  } catch (error) {\n    await log(`   ❌ Enhanced fetch failed: ${cleanErrorMessage(error)}`, { level: 'error' });\n    // Check if this is a rate limit error - if so, re-throw immediately\n    if (isRateLimitError(error)) {\n      await log('   ⚠️  Rate limit detected - re-throwing for caller to handle', { verbose: true });\n      throw error;\n    }\n    // Check if this is the \"hit search API limit\" error - if so, re-throw to trigger repository fallback\n    const errorMsg = error.message || error.toString();\n    if (errorMsg.includes('Hit search API limit') || errorMsg.includes('repository-by-repository fallback')) {\n      await log('   🔄 Re-throwing error to trigger repository-by-repository fallback...', { verbose: true });\n      throw error;\n    }\n    // For other errors, try a simple fallback with default limit\n    try {\n      await log('   🔄 Falling back to default behavior...', { verbose: true });\n      const fallbackCommand = baseCommand.includes('--limit') ? baseCommand : `${baseCommand} --limit 100`;\n      await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, timeouts.githubRepoDelay)); // Shorter delay for fallback\n      // #1756: use execGhWithRetry on fallback too\n      const { stdout } = await execGhWithRetry(fallbackCommand, {\n        execOptions: { encoding: 'utf8', env: process.env },\n        label: 'gh search/list issues (fallback)',\n      });\n      const issues = JSON.parse(stdout || '[]');\n      await log(`   ⚠️  Fallback: fetched ${issues.length} issues (limited to 100)`, { level: 'warning' });\n      return issues;\n    } catch (fallbackError) {\n      await log(`   ❌ Fallback also failed: ${cleanErrorMessage(fallbackError)}`, { level: 'error' });\n      // Re-throw the error so the caller can handle it appropriately\n      throw fallbackError;\n    }\n  }\n}\n// Function to fetch issues from GitHub Projects v2\nexport async function fetchProjectIssues(projectNumber, owner, statusFilter) {\n  try {\n    await log(`🔍 Fetching issues from GitHub Project #${projectNumber} (owner: ${owner}, status: ${statusFilter})`);\n    // Check for project scope in GitHub CLI authentication\n    try {\n      const authStatus = await $`gh auth status --show-token`;\n      if (!authStatus.stdout.includes('project')) {\n        throw new Error('Missing project scope. Run: gh auth refresh -s project');\n      }\n    } catch (error) {\n      reportError(error, {\n        context: 'github.lib.mjs - GitHub CLI auth status check',\n        level: 'error',\n      });\n      throw new Error('GitHub CLI authentication failed. Please run: gh auth login', { cause: error });\n    }\n    // Add delay to respect rate limits\n    await log('   ⏰ Waiting 2 seconds before API call to respect rate limits...', { verbose: true });\n    await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, timeouts.githubRepoDelay));\n    const startTime = Date.now();\n    // Fetch all project items\n    await log(`   🔎 Executing: gh project item-list ${projectNumber} --owner ${owner} --format json --limit 100`, {\n      verbose: true,\n    });\n    const result = await $`gh project item-list ${projectNumber} --owner ${owner} --format json --limit 100`;\n    const endTime = Date.now();\n    const projectData = JSON.parse(result.stdout || '{\"items\": []}');\n    const allItems = projectData.items || [];\n    await log(`   📊 Found ${allItems.length} total project items in ${Math.round((endTime - startTime) / 1000)}s`);\n    // Filter by status and item type (only Issues)\n    const filteredIssues = allItems.filter(item => {\n      // Check if it's an Issue (not PR, Discussion, etc.)\n      if (item.content?.type !== 'Issue') {\n        return false;\n      }\n      // Check status field - look for Status field in fieldValueByName\n      const statusField = item.fieldValueByName?.Status;\n      if (!statusField) {\n        // If no status field, skip this item\n        return false;\n      }\n      // Match against configured status value\n      return statusField.name === statusFilter;\n    });\n    // Extract issue information\n    const issues = filteredIssues.map(item => ({\n      url: item.content.url,\n      title: item.content.title,\n      number: item.content.number,\n      repository: item.content.repository,\n      labels: item.content.labels || [],\n      state: item.content.state || 'open',\n    }));\n    await log(`   ✅ Found ${issues.length} issues with status \"${statusFilter}\"`);\n    if (issues.length > 0) {\n      await log('   📋 Issues found:', { log('   ⏰ Adding 2-second delay after API call to respect rate limits...', { verbose: true });\n    await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, timeouts.githubRepoDelay));\n    return issues;\n  } catch (error) {\n    await log(`   ❌ Failed to fetch project issues: ${cleanErrorMessage(error)}`, { level: 'error' });\n    // Provide helpful error messages for common issues\n    if (error.message.includes('project scope')) {\n      await log('   💡 To fix this, run: gh auth refresh -s project', { level: 'info' });\n    } else if (error.message.includes('authentication')) {\n      await log('   💡 To fix this, run: gh auth login', { level: 'info' });\n    } else if (error.message.includes('not found') || error.message.includes('404')) {\n      await log('   💡 Check that the project number and owner are correct', { level: 'info' });\n      await log('   💡 Make sure you have access to the project', { level: 'info' });\n    }\n    return [];\n  }\n}\n// Re-export batch operations from separate module\nexport const batchCheckPullRequestsForIssues = batchCheckPRs;\n/**\n * Universal GitHub URL parser that handles various formats\n * @param {string} url - The GitHub URL to parse\n * @returns {Object} Parsed URL information including:\n *   - valid: boolean indicating if the URL is valid\n *   - normalized: the normalized URL (https://github.com/...)\n *   - type: 'user', 'repo', 'issue', 'pull', 'gist', 'actions', etc.\n *   - owner: repository owner/organization\n *   - repo: repository name (if applicable)\n *   - number: issue/PR number (if applicable)\n *   - path: additional path components\n *   - error: error message if invalid\n */\nexport function parseGitHubUrl(url) {\n  if (!url || typeof url !== 'string') {\n    return {\n      valid: false,\n      error: 'Invalid input: URL must be a non-empty string',\n    };\n  }\n  // Trim whitespace and remove trailing slashes\n  let normalizedUrl = url.trim().replace(/\\/+$/, '');\n  // Check if this looks like a valid GitHub-related input\n  // Reject clearly invalid inputs (spaces in the URL, special chars at the start, etc.)\n  if (/\\s/.test(normalizedUrl) || /^[!@#$%^&*()[\\]{}|\\\\:;\"'<>,?`~]/.test(normalizedUrl)) {\n    return {\n      valid: false,\n      error: 'Invalid GitHub URL format',\n    };\n  }\n  // Handle protocol normalization\n  if (!normalizedUrl.startsWith('http://') && !normalizedUrl.startsWith('https://')) {\n    // Check if it starts with github.com\n    if (normalizedUrl.startsWith('github.com/')) {\n      normalizedUrl = 'https://' + normalizedUrl;\n    } else if (!normalizedUrl.includes('github.com')) {\n      // Assume it's a shorthand format (owner, owner/repo, owner/repo/issues/123, etc.)\n      normalizedUrl = 'https://github.com/' + normalizedUrl;\n    } else {\n      // Has github.com somewhere but not at the start - likely malformed\n      return {\n        valid: false,\n        error: 'Invalid GitHub URL format',\n      };\n    }\n  }\n  // Convert http to https\n  if (normalizedUrl.startsWith('http://')) {\n    normalizedUrl = normalizedUrl.replace(/^http:\\/\\//, 'https://');\n  }\n\n  // Check for backslashes in the URL path (excluding query params and hash)\n  // According to RFC 3986, backslash is not a valid character in URL paths\n  const urlBeforeQueryAndHash = normalizedUrl.split('?')[0].split('#')[0];\n  if (urlBeforeQueryAndHash.includes('\\\\')) {\n    // Generate suggested URL by replacing backslashes with forward slashes\n    const suggestedUrl = urlBeforeQueryAndHash.replace(/\\\\/g, '/');\n    const urlAfterPath = normalizedUrl.substring(urlBeforeQueryAndHash.length);\n\n    return {\n      valid: false,\n      error: 'Invalid character in URL: backslash (\\\\) is not allowed in URL paths',\n      suggestion: suggestedUrl + urlAfterPath,\n    };\n  }\n\n  // Parse the URL\n  let urlObj;\n  try {\n    urlObj = new globalThis.URL(normalizedUrl);\n  } catch (e) {\n    if (global.verboseMode) {\n      reportError(e, {\n        context: 'github.lib.mjs - URL parsing',\n        level: 'debug',\n        url: normalizedUrl,\n      });\n    }\n    return {\n      valid: false,\n      error: 'Invalid URL format',\n    };\n  }\n  // Ensure it's a GitHub URL\n  if (urlObj.hostname !== 'github.com' && urlObj.hostname !== 'www.github.com') {\n    return {\n      valid: false,\n      error: 'Not a GitHub URL',\n    };\n  }\n  // Normalize hostname\n  if (urlObj.hostname === 'www.github.com') {\n    normalizedUrl = normalizedUrl.replace('www.github.com', 'github.com');\n    urlObj = new globalThis.URL(normalizedUrl);\n  }\n  // Parse the pathname\n  const pathParts = urlObj.pathname.split('/').filter(p => p);\n  // Handle different GitHub URL patterns\n  const result = {\n    valid: true,\n    normalized: normalizedUrl,\n    hostname: 'github.com',\n    protocol: 'https',\n    path: urlObj.pathname,\n  };\n  // No path - just github.com\n  if (pathParts.length === 0) {\n    result.type = 'home';\n    return result;\n  }\n  // User/Organization page: /owner\n  if (pathParts.length === 1) {\n    result.type = 'user';\n    result.owner = pathParts[0];\n    return result;\n  }\n  // Set owner for all other cases\n  result.owner = pathParts[0];\n  // Repository page: /owner/repo\n  if (pathParts.length === 2) {\n    result.type = 'repo';\n    result.repo = pathParts[1];\n    return result;\n  }\n  // Set repo for paths with 3+ parts\n  result.repo = pathParts[1];\n  // Handle specific GitHub paths\n  const thirdPart = pathParts[2];\n  switch (thirdPart) {\n    case 'issues':\n      if (pathParts.length === 3) {\n        // /owner/repo/issues - issues list\n        result.type = 'issues_list';\n      } else if (pathParts.length === 4 && /^\\d+$/.test(pathParts[3])) {\n        // /owner/repo/issues/123 - specific issue\n        result.type = 'issue';\n        result.number = parseInt(pathParts[3]);\n      } else {\n        result.type = 'issues_page';\n        result.subpath = pathParts.slice(3).join('/');\n      }\n      break;\n    case 'pull':\n      if (pathParts.length === 4 && /^\\d+$/.test(pathParts[3])) {\n        // /owner/repo/pull/456 - specific PR\n        result.type = 'pull';\n        result.number = parseInt(pathParts[3]);\n      } else {\n        result.type = 'pull_page';\n        result.subpath = pathParts.slice(3).join('/');\n      }\n      break;\n    case 'pulls':\n      // /owner/repo/pulls - PR list\n      result.type = 'pulls_list';\n      if (pathParts.length > 3) {\n        result.subpath = pathParts.slice(3).join('/');\n      }\n      break;\n    case 'actions':\n      // /owner/repo/actions - GitHub Actions\n      result.type = 'actions';\n      if (pathParts.length > 3) {\n        result.subpath = pathParts.slice(3).join('/');\n        if (pathParts[3] === 'runs' && pathParts[4] && /^\\d+$/.test(pathParts[4])) {\n          result.type = 'action_run';\n          result.runId = parseInt(pathParts[4]);\n        }\n      }\n      break;\n    case 'releases':\n      // /owner/repo/releases\n      result.type = 'releases';\n      if (pathParts.length > 3) {\n        result.subpath = pathParts.slice(3).join('/');\n        if (pathParts[3] === 'tag' && pathParts[4]) {\n          result.type = 'release';\n          result.tag = pathParts[4];\n        }\n      }\n      break;\n    case 'tree':\n    case 'blob':\n      // /owner/repo/tree/branch or /owner/repo/blob/branch/file\n      result.type = thirdPart === 'tree' ? 'tree' : 'file';\n      if (pathParts.length > 3) {\n        result.branch = pathParts[3];\n        if (pathParts.length > 4) {\n          result.filepath = pathParts.slice(4).join('/');\n        }\n      }\n      break;\n    case 'commit':\n    case 'commits':\n      // /owner/repo/commit/sha or /owner/repo/commits/branch\n      result.type = thirdPart === 'commit' ? 'commit' : 'commits';\n      if (pathParts.length > 3) {\n        result.ref = pathParts[3]; // Could be SHA or branch\n      }\n      break;\n    case 'compare':\n      // /owner/repo/compare/base...head\n      result.type = 'compare';\n      if (pathParts.length > 3) {\n        result.comparison = pathParts[3];\n      }\n      break;\n    case 'wiki':\n      // /owner/repo/wiki\n      result.type = 'wiki';\n      if (pathParts.length > 3) {\n        result.subpath = pathParts.slice(3).join('/');\n      }\n      break;\n    case 'settings':\n      // /owner/repo/settings\n      result.type = 'settings';\n      if (pathParts.length > 3) {\n        result.subpath = pathParts.slice(3).join('/');\n      }\n      break;\n    case 'projects':\n      // /owner/repo/projects or /owner/repo/projects/1\n      result.type = 'projects';\n      if (pathParts.length > 3 && /^\\d+$/.test(pathParts[3])) {\n        result.type = 'project';\n        result.projectNumber = parseInt(pathParts[3]);\n      }\n      break;\n    default:\n      // Unknown path structure but still valid GitHub URL\n      result.type = 'other';\n      result.subpath = pathParts.slice(2).join('/');\n  }\n  return result;\n}\n/**\n * Normalize a GitHub URL to standard https://github.com format\n * This is a convenience function that uses parseGitHubUrl\n * @param {string} url - The URL to normalize\n * @returns {string|null} The normalized URL or null if invalid\n */\nexport function normalizeGitHubUrl(url) {\n  const parsed = parseGitHubUrl(url);\n  return parsed.valid ? parsed.normalized : null;\n}\n/**\n * Check if a URL is a valid GitHub URL of a specific type\n * @param {string} url - The URL to check\n * @param {string|Array} types - The type(s) to check for ('issue', 'pull', 'repo', etc.)\n * @returns {boolean} True if the URL matches the specified type(s)\n */\nexport function isGitHubUrlType(url, types) {\n  const parsed = parseGitHubUrl(url);\n  if (!parsed.valid) return false;\n  const typeArray = Array.isArray(types) ? types : [types];\n  return typeArray.includes(parsed.type);\n}\n/**\n * Universal function to view @returns {Promise<{code: number, stdout: string, stderr: string, data: Object|null}>}\n */\nexport async function ghPrView({ prNumber, owner, repo, jsonFields = !(stderr && stderr.includes('Could not resolve'))) {\n      try {\n        data = JSON.parse(stdout);\n      } catch {\n        // If JSON parsing fails, data remains null\n      }\n    }\n    return {\n      code,\n      stdout,\n      stderr,\n      data,\n      output: stdout + stderr,\n    };\n  } catch (error) {\n    return {\n      code: error.code || 1,\n      stdout: error.stdout?.toString() || '',\n      stderr: error.stderr?.toString() || error.message || '',\n      data: null,\n      output: (error.stdout?.toString() || '') + (error.stderr?.toString() || error.message || ''),\n    };\n  }\n}\n/**\n * Universal function to view an issue using gh issue view\n * @param {Object} options - Configuration options\n * @param {number|string} [options.jsonFields='number,title'] - JSON fields to return\n * @returns {Promise<{code: number, stdout: string, stderr: string, data: Object|null}>}\n */\nexport async function ghIssueView({ return {\n      code,\n      stdout,\n      stderr,\n      data,\n      output: stdout + stderr,\n    };\n  } catch (error) {\n    return {\n      code: error.code || 1,\n      stdout: error.stdout?.toString() || '',\n      stderr: error.stderr?.toString() || error.message || '',\n      data: null,\n      output: (error.stdout?.toString() || '') + (error.stderr?.toString() || error.message || ''),\n    };\n  }\n}\n/**\n * Handle PR not found error and check if an issue exists with the same number\n * Provides user-friendly error messages and command suggestions\n * @param {Object} options - Configuration options\n * @param {number} options.prNumber - PR number that doesn't exist\n * @param {string} options.owner - Repository owner\n * @param {string} options.repo - Repository name\n * @param {Object} options.argv - Command line arguments object (for reconstructing command)\n * @param {boolean} [options.shouldAttachLogs] - Whether --attach-logs was used\n * @returns {Promise<void>}\n */\nexport async function handlePRNotFoundError({ prNumber, owner, repo, argv, shouldAttachLogs }) {\n  await log(`Error: PR #${prNumber} does not exist in ${owner}/${repo}`, { level: 'error' });\n  await log('', { level: 'error' });\n  try {\n    const issueCheckResult = await ghIssueView({ issueNumber: prNumber, owner, repo, jsonFields: 'number,title' });\n    if (issueCheckResult.code === 0 && issueCheckResult.data) {\n      await log(`💡 However, Issue #${prNumber} exists with the same number:`, { level: 'error' });\n      await log(`   Title: \"${issueCheckResult.data.title}\"`, { level: 'error' });\n      await log('', { level: 'error' });\n      await log('🔧 Did you mean to work on the issue instead?', { level: 'error' });\n      await In\n      * a container where `~/.gitconfig` is bind-mounted, git cannot replace it and\n      * gh reports `failed to set up git credential helper: failed to run git: error:\n      * could not write config file /home/box/.gitconfig: Device or resource busy`.\n      * Hive Mind used to mirror that line raw and continue with no credential helper\n      * at all, so the real failure only surfaced later as a push error.\n      *\n      * The clone-local config is equivalent for our purposes and is never\n      * bind-mounted, so it is used as the fallback. The empty `helper` entry first\n      * clears any inherited helper, exactly as `gh auth setup-git` does.\n      */\n     export async function setupGitCredentialHelper({ tempDir, log, $, hosts = ['github.com'] }) {\n       const authSetupResult = await $({ cwd: tempDir, mirror: false, capture: true })`gh auth setup-git 2>&1`;\n       if (authSetupResult.code === 0) return { scope: 'global', hosts };\n\n       const reason = (authSetupResult.stdout?.toString() || authSetupResult.stderr?.toString() || '').trim();\n       await log(`ℹ️  gh auth setup-git could not write the global gitconfig${reason ? `: ${reason.split('\\n')[0]}` : ''}`, { verbose: true });\n\n       const failures = [];\n       for (const host of hosts) {\n         const key = `credential.https://${host}.helper`;\n         const cleared = await $({ cwd: tempDir, mirror: false, capture: true })`git config --local --replace-all ${key} \"\"`;\n         const configured = await $({ cwd: tempDir, mirror: false, capture: true })`git config --local --add ${key} ${'!gh auth git-credential'}`;\n         if (cleared.code !== 0 || configured.code !== 0) failures.push(host);\n       }\n\n       if (failures.length) {\n         await log(`⚠️  Could not configure a git credential helper for ${failures.join(', ')} - pushes may require credentials in the remote URL`, { level: 'warning' });\n         return { scope: 'none', hosts: failures };\n       }\n\n       await log('🔑 Configured the gh credential helper for this clone (the global gitconfig is not writable)', { verbose: true });\n       return { scope: 'local', hosts };\n     }\n     ```\n\n   - **`experiments/issue-2130/e2e-direct-endpoint.mjs`** — committed.     "originalFile": "#!/usr/bin/env node\n\n/**\n * GitHub API rate-limit detection and retry utilities.\n *\n * Issue #1726: Hosted runners hit GitHub's 5,000/hr core API quota and bubble\n * the failure up as a generic 403/HTTP error. The wrappers in lib.mjs only\n * recognise transient TCP/TLS faults; rate-limit responses fell through and\n * crashed callers (or worse, were silently swallowed in the merge subsystem\n * making it look like \"no workflows / no checks\" — see\n * src/github-merge.lib.mjs:getActiveRepoWorkflows in the original log).\n *\n * The retry policy required by the issue:\n *   wait = (resetTimestamp - now) + bufferMs (10 min) + random(jitterMs) (0-5 min)\n *\n * `bufferMs` and `jitterMs` already exist in src/config.lib.mjs#limitReset\n * (added in #1236 for Claude limit waits) so we re-use them rather than\n * duplicate constants.\n */\nimport { promisify } from 'node:util';\nimport { exec as execCb } from 'node:child_process';\n\nimport { limitReset, retryLimits } from './config.lib.mjs';\n\nconst exec = promisify(execCb);\n\nconst GITHUB_RATE_LIMIT_USAGE_RESOURCES = ['core', 'graphql', 'search'];\nconst RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS = ['api rate limit exceeded', 'rate limit exceeded', 'you have exceeded a secondary rate limit', 'secondary rate limit', 'abuse detection', 'was submitted too quickly'];\n\nconst githubRateLimitLogging = {\n  enabled: false,\n  log: null,\n  fetchUsage: null,\n  lastUsageByResource: null,\n};\n\n/**\n * Pull every plausible string out of a thrown error/result so pattern matches\n * survive whatever shape the upstream caller gave us (Error, exec result with\n * stdout/stderr, command-stream result, plain string, etc.).\n */\nconst collectErrorText = error => {\n  if (!error) return '';\n  if (typeof error === 'string') return error;\n  const parts = [];\n  if (typeof error.message === 'string') parts.push(error.message);\n  if (typeof error.stderr === 'string') parts.push(error.stderr);\n  else if (error.stderr && typeof error.stderr.toString === 'function') parts.push(error.stderr.toString());\n  if (typeof error.stdout === 'string') parts.push(error.stdout);\n  else if (error.stdout && typeof error.stdout.toString === 'function') parts.push(error.stdout.toString());\n  if (error.cause) parts.push(collectErrorText(error.cause));\n  return parts.join('\\n');\n};\n\n/**\n * Detect whether `error` represents a GitHub rate-limit response.\n * Recognises both primary (5,000/hr) and secondary (abuse-detection) forms.\n *\n * @param {unknown} error\n * @returns {boolean}\n */\nexport const isRateLimitError = error => {\n  const text = collectErrorText(error).toLowerCase();\n  if (!text) return false;\n  return RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS.some(pattern => text.includes(pattern));\n};\n\n/**\n * Extract a `Date` for when the rate-limit window resets, in priority order:\n *   1. `X-RateLimit-Reset` header value (Unix epoch seconds) embedded in the\n *      error text — `gh` prints headers when --include is used The error to check\n * @returns {boolean} True if the error indicates rate limiting\n */\nexport function isRateLimitError(error) {\n  const errorMessage = (error.message || error.toString()).toLowerCase();\n  // Common rate limit error patterns\n  const rateLimitPatterns = ['rate limit', 'secondary rate limit', 'exceeded.*limit', 'too many requests', 'abuse detection', 'wait a few minutes', 'http 403.*rate', 'api rate limit exceeded'];\n  return rateLimitPatterns.some(pattern => {\n    return new RegExp(pattern).test(errorMessage);\n  });\n}\n/**\n * Helper function to fetch all issues with pagination and rate limiting\n * Note: GitHub Search API has a hard limit of 1000 results total.\n * For user/org queries with >1000 issues, the fetchIssuesFromRepositories fallback should be used.\n * @param {string} baseCommand - The base gh command to execute\n * @returns {Promise<Array>} Array of issues\n */\nexport async function fetchAllIssuesWithPagination(baseCommand) {\n  // Import log and cleanErrorMessage from lib.mjs\n  const { log, cleanErrorMessage } = await import('./lib.mjs');\n  try {\n    // First, try without pagination to see if we get more than the default limit\n    await log('   📊 Fetching issues with improved limits and rate limiting...', { verbose: true });\n    // Add a 5-second delay before making the API call to respect rate limits\n    await log('   ⏰ Waiting 5 seconds before API call to respect rate limits...', { verbose: true });\n    await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, timeouts.githubApiDelay));\n    const startTime = Date.now();\n    // Use appropriate page sizes: 100 for search API (more restrictive), 1000 for regular listing\n    const commandWithoutLimit = baseCommand.replace(/--limit\\s+\\d+/, '');\n    const isSearchCommand = commandWithoutLimit.includes('gh search');\n    const maxPageSize = isSearchCommand ? 100 : 1000;\n    const improvedCommand = `${commandWithoutLimit} --limit ${maxPageSize}`;\n    await log(`   🔎 Executing: ${improvedCommand}`, { verbose: true });\n    // #1756: use execGhWithRetry so transient 5xx (e.g., 504) auto-retry\n    const { stdout } = await execGhWithRetry(improvedCommand, {\n      execOptions: { encoding: 'utf8', env: process.env },\n      label: 'gh search/list issues (paginated)',\n    });\n    const endTime = Date.now();\n    const issues = JSON.parse(stdout || '[]');\n    await log(`   ✅ Fetched ${issues.length} issues in ${Math.round((endTime - startTime) / 1000)}s`);\n    // If we got exactly the max page size, there might be more - log a warning and throw error to trigger fallback\n    if (issues.length === maxPageSize) {\n      await log(`   ⚠️  Hit the ${maxPageSize} issue limit - there may be more issues available`, { level: 'warning' });\n      if (isSearchCommand) {\n        await log('   💡 GitHub Search API is limited to 1000 results max. Triggering repository fallback for complete results.', { level: 'info' });\n        // Throw an error to trigger the fallback to fetchIssuesFromRepositories which uses GraphQL pagination\n        throw new Error(`Hit search API limit of ${maxPageSize} issues - need repository-by-repository fallback for complete results`);\n      } else if (maxPageSize >= 1000) {\n        await log(`   💡 Consider filtering by labels or date ranges for repositories with >${maxPageSize} open issues`, { level: 'info' });\n      }\n    }\n    // Add a 5-second delay after the call to be extra safe with rate limits\n    await log('   ⏰ Adding 5-second delay after API call to respect rate limits...', { verbose: true });\n    await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, timeouts.githubApiDelay));\n    return issues;\n  } catch (error) {\n    await log(`   ❌ Enhanced fetch failed: ${cleanErrorMessage(error)}`, { level: 'error' });\n    // Check if this is a rate limit error - if so, re-throw immediately\n    if (isRateLimitError(error)) {\n      await log('   ⚠️  Rate limit detected - re-throwing for caller to handle', { verbose: true });\n      throw error;\n    }\n    // Check if this is the \"hit search API limit\" error - if so, re-throw to trigger repository fallback\n    const errorMsg = error.message || error.toString();\n    if (errorMsg.includes('Hit search API limit') || errorMsg.includes('repository-by-repository fallback')) {\n      await log('   🔄 Re-throwing error to trigger repository-by-repository fallback...', { verbose: true });\n      throw error;\n    }\n    // For other errors, try a simple fallback with default limit\n    try {\n      await log('   🔄 Falling back to default behavior...', { verbose: true });\n      const fallbackCommand = baseCommand.includes('--limit') ? baseCommand : `${baseCommand} --limit 100`;\n      await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, timeouts.githubRepoDelay)); // Shorter delay for fallback\n      // #1756: use execGhWithRetry on fallback too\n      const { stdout } = await execGhWithRetry(fallbackCommand, {\n        execOptions: { encoding: 'utf8', env: process.env },\n        label: 'gh search/list issues (fallback)',\n      });\n      const issues = JSON.parse(stdout || '[]');\n      await log(`   ⚠️  Fallback: fetched ${issues.length} issues (limited to 100)`, { level: 'warning' });\n      return issues;\n    } catch (fallbackError) {\n      await log(`   ❌ Fallback also failed: ${cleanErrorMessage(fallbackError)}`, { level: 'error' });\n      // Re-throw the error so the caller can handle it appropriately\n      throw fallbackError;\n    }\n  }\n}\n// Function to fetch issues from GitHub Projects v2\nexport async function fetchProjectIssues(projectNumber, owner, statusFilter) {\n  try {\n    await log(`🔍 Fetching issues from GitHub Project #${projectNumber} (owner: ${owner}, status: ${statusFilter})`);\n    // Check for project scope in GitHub CLI authentication\n    try {\n      const authStatus = await $`gh auth status --show-token`;\n      if (!authStatus.stdout.includes('project')) {\n        throw new Error('Missing project scope. Run: gh auth refresh -s project');\n      }\n    } catch (error) {\n      reportError(error, {\n        context: 'github.lib.mjs - GitHub CLI auth status check',\n        level: 'error',\n      });\n      throw new Error('GitHub CLI authentication failed. Please run: gh auth login', { cause: error });\n    }\n    // Add delay to respect rate limits\n    await log('   ⏰ Waiting 2 seconds before API call to respect rate limits...', { verbose: true });\n    await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, timeouts.githubRepoDelay));\n    const startTime = Date.now();\n    // Fetch all project items\n    await log(`   🔎 Executing: gh project item-list ${projectNumber} --owner ${owner} --format json --limit 100`, {\n      verbose: true,\n    });\n    const result = await $`gh project item-list ${projectNumber} --owner ${owner} --format json --limit 100`;\n    const endTime = Date.now();\n    const projectData = JSON.parse(result.stdout || '{\"items\": []}');\n    const allItems = projectData.items || [];\n    await log(`   📊 Found ${allItems.length} total project items in ${Math.round((endTime - startTime) / 1000)}s`);\n    // Filter by status and item type (only Issues)\n    const filteredIssues = allItems.filter(item => {\n      // Check if it's an Issue (not PR, Discussion, etc.)\n      if (item.content?.type !== 'Issue') {\n        return false;\n      }\n      // Check status field - look for Status field in fieldValueByName\n      const statusField = item.fieldValueByName?.Status;\n      if (!statusField) {\n        // If no status field, skip this item\n        return false;\n      }\n      // Match against configured status value\n      return statusField.name === statusFilter;\n    });\n    // Extract issue information\n    const issues = filteredIssues.map(item => ({\n      url: item.content.url,\n      title: item.content.title,\n      number: item.content.number,\n      repository: item.content.repository,\n      labels: item.content.labels || [],\n      state: item.content.state || 'open',\n    }));\n    await log(`   ✅ Found ${issues.length} issues with status \"${statusFilter}\"`);\n    if (issues.length > 0) {\n      await log('   📋 Issues found:', { verbose: true });\n      for (const issue of issues) {\n        await log(`      • #${issue.number}: ${issue.title}`, { verbose: true });\n      }\n    }\n    // Add delay after API call\n    await log('   ⏰ Adding 2-second delay after API call to respect rate limits...', { verbose: true });\n    await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, timeouts.githubRepoDelay));\n    return issues;\n  } catch (error) {\n    await log(`   ❌ Failed to fetch project issues: ${cleanErrorMessage(error)}`, { level: 'error' });\n    // Provide helpful error messages for common issues\n    if (error.message.includes('project scope')) {\n      await log('   💡 To fix this, run: gh auth refresh -s project', { level: 'info' });\n    } else if (error.message.includes('authentication')) {\n operations from separate module\nexport const batchCheckPullRequestsForIssues = batchCheckPRs;\n/**\n * Universal GitHub URL parser that handles various formats\n * @param {string} url - The GitHub    error: 'Invalid input: URL must be a non-empty string',\n    };\n  }\n  // Trim whitespace and remove trailing slashes\n  let normalizedUrl = url.trim().replace(/\\/+$/, '');\n  // Check if this looks like a valid GitHub-related input\n  // Reject clearly invalid inputs (spaces in the URL, special chars at the start, etc.)\n  if (/\\s/.test(normalizedUrl) || /^[!@#$%^&*()[\\]{}|\\\\:;\"'<>,?`~]/.test(normalizedUrl)) {\n    return {\n      valid: false,\n      error: 'Invalid GitHub URL format',\n    };\n  }\n  // Handle protocol normalization\n  if (!normalizedUrl.startsWith('http://') && !normalizedUrl.startsWith('https://')) {\n    // Check if it starts with github.com\n    if (normalizedUrl.startsWith('github.com/')) {\n      normalizedUrl = 'https://' + normalizedUrl;\n    } else if (!normalizedUrl.includes('github.com')) {\n      // Assume it's a shorthand format (owner, owner/repo, owner/repo/issues/123, etc.)\n      normalizedUrl = 'https://github.com/' + normalizedUrl;\n    } else {\n      // Has github.com somewhere but not at the start - likely malformed\n      return {\n        valid: false,\n        error: 'Invalid GitHub for backslashes in the URL path (excluding query params and hash)\n  // According to RFC 3986, backslash is not a valid character in URL paths\n  const urlBeforeQueryAndHash = normalizedUrl.split('?')[0].split('#')[0];\n  if (urlBeforeQueryAndHash.includes('\\\\')) {\n    // Generate suggested URL by replacing backslashes with forward slashes\n    const suggestedUrl = urlBeforeQueryAndHash.replace(/\\\\/g, '/');\n    const urlAfterPath = normalizedUrl.substring(urlBeforeQueryAndHash.length);\n\n    return {\n      valid: false,\n      error: 'Invalid character in URL: backslash (\\\\) is not allowed in URL paths',\n      suggestion: suggestedUrl + urlAfterPath,\n    };\n  }\n\n  // Parse the URL\n  let urlObj;\n  try {\n    urlObj = new globalThis.URL(normalizedUrl);\n  } catch (e) {\n    if (global.verboseMode) {\n      reportError(e, {\n        context: 'github.lib.mjs - URL parsing',\n        level: 'debug',\n        url: normalizedUrl,\n      });\n    }\n    return {\n      valid: false,\n      error: 'Invalid URL format',\n    };\n  }\n  // Ensure it's a GitHub URL\n  if (urlObj.hostname !== 'github.com' && pathParts[1];\n  // Handle specific GitHub paths\n  const thirdPart = pathParts[2];\n  switch (thirdPart) {\n    case 'issues':\n      if (pathParts.length === 3) {\n        // /owner/repo/issues - 'Pull Request' : 'Issue';\n  const ghCommand = targetType === 'pr' ? 'pr' : 'issue';\n  void ghCommand;\n  const logStats = await fs.stat(logFile);\n\n  const tempFile = `/tmp/log-comment-${targetType}-${Date.now()}.md`;\n  await writeSanitizedPublicationFile(tempFile, logComment);\n\n  // Issue #1625: track the posted comment ID so it's excluded from the\n  // AI-authored-comment check in --auto-attach-solution-summary.\n  let posted;\n  try {\n    posted = await postTrackedCommentFromFile({ $, owner, repo, targetNumber, bodyFile: tempFile });\n  } finally {\n    await fs.unlink(tempFile).catch(() => {});\n  }\n\n  if (posted.ok) {\n    const status = getLogUploadTerminalStatus({ errorMessage, errorDuringExecution, isUsageLimit });\n    await log(`  ${status.emoji} ${status.label} uploaded to ${targetName} as comment${posted.commentId ? ` (id=${posted.commentId})` : ''}`);\n    await log(`  📊 Log size: ${Math.round(logStats.size / 1024)}KB`);\n    return true;\n  } else {\n    await log(`  ❌ Failed to upload log to ${targetName}: ${posted.stderr || 'unknown error'}`);\n    return false;\n  }\n}\n/**\n * Detects if an error is due to GitHub API rate limiting\n * @param {Error|string} error - The error to check\n * @returns {boolean} True if the error indicates rate limiting\n */\nexport function isRateLimitError(error) {\n  const errorMessage = (error.message || error.toString()).toLowerCase();\n  // Common rate limit error patterns\n  const rateLimitPatterns = ['rate limit', 'secondary rate limit', 'exceeded.*limit', 'too many requests', 'abuse detection', 'wait a few minutes', 'http 403.*rate', 'api rate limit exceeded'];\n  return rateLimitPatterns.some(pattern => {\n    return new RegExp(pattern).test(errorMessage);\n  });\n}\n/**\n * Helper function to fetch all issues with pagination and rate limiting\n * Note: GitHub Search API has a hard limit of 1000 results total.\n * For user/org queries with >1000 issues, the fetchIssuesFromRepositories fallback should be used.\n * @param {string} baseCommand - The base gh command to execute\n * @returns {Promise<Array>} Array of issues\n */\nexport async function fetchAllIssuesWithPagination(baseCommand) {\n  // Import log and cleanErrorMessage from lib.mjs\n  const { log, cleanErrorMessage } = await import('./lib.mjs');\n  try {\n    // First, try without pagination to see if we get more than the default limit\n    await log('   📊 Fetching issues with improved limits and rate limiting...', { verbose: true });\n    // Add a 5-second delay before making the API call to respect rate limits\n    await log('   ⏰ Waiting 5 seconds before API call to respect rate limits...', { verbose: true });\n    await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, timeouts.githubApiDelay));\n    const startTime = Date.now();\n    // Use appropriate page sizes: 100 for search API (more restrictive), 1000 for regular listing\n    const commandWithoutLimit = baseCommand.replace(/--limit\\s+\\d+/, '');\n    const isSearchCommand = commandWithoutLimit.includes('gh search');\n    const maxPageSize = isSearchCommand ? 100 : 1000;\n    const improvedCommand = `${commandWithoutLimit} --limit ${maxPageSize}`;\n    await log(`   🔎 Executing: ${improvedCommand}`, { verbose: true });\n    // #1756: use execGhWithRetry so transient 5xx (e.g., 504) auto-retry\n    const { stdout } = await execGhWithRetry(improvedCommand, {\n      execOptions: { encoding: 'utf8', env: process.env },\n      label: 'gh search/list issues (paginated)',\n    });\n    const endTime = Date.now();\n    const issues = JSON.parse(stdout || '[]');\n    await log(`   ✅ Fetched ${issues.length} issues in ${Math.round((endTime - startTime) / 1000)}s`);\n    // If we got exactly the max page size, there might be more - log a warning and throw error to trigger fallback\n    if (issues.length === maxPageSize) {\n      await log(`   ⚠️  Hit the ${maxPageSize} issue limit - there may be more issues available`, { level: 'warning' });\n      if (isSearchCommand) {\n        await log('   💡 GitHub Search API is limited to 1000 results max. Triggering repository fallback for complete results.', { level: 'info' });\n        // Throw an error to trigger the fallback to fetchIssuesFromRepositories which uses GraphQL pagination\n        throw new Error(`Hit search API limit of ${maxPageSize} issues - need repository-by-repository fallback for complete results`);\n      } else if (maxPageSize >= 1000) {\n        await log(`   💡 Consider filtering by labels or date ranges for repositories with >${maxPageSize} open issues`, { level: 'info' });\n      }\n    }\n    // Add a 5-second delay after the call to be extra safe with rate limits\n    await log('   ⏰ Adding 5-second delay after API call to respect rate limits...', { verbose: true });\n    await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, timeouts.githubApiDelay));\n    return issues;\n  } catch (error) {\n    await log(`   ❌ Enhanced fetch failed: ${cleanErrorMessage(error)}`, { level: 'error' });\n    // Check if this is a rate limit error - if so, re-throw immediately\n    if (isRateLimitError(error)) {\n      await log('   ⚠️  Rate limit detected - re-throwing for caller to handle', { verbose: true });\n      throw error;\n    }\n    // Check if this is the \"hit search API limit\" error - if so, re-throw to trigger repository fallback\n    const errorMsg = error.message || error.toString();\n    if (errorMsg.includes('Hit search API limit') || errorMsg.includes('repository-by-repository fallback')) {\n      await log('   🔄 Re-throwing error to trigger repository-by-repository fallback...', { verbose: true });\n      throw error;\n    }\n    // For other errors, try a simple fallback with default limit\n    try {\n      await log('   🔄 Falling back to default behavior...', { verbose: true });\n      const fallbackCommand = baseCommand.includes('--limit') ? These patterns let\n * callers recognise the transient case and degrade gracefully instead.\n *\n * Note: HTTP 500 is deliberately matched here (and NOT in\n * `TRANSIENT_NETWORK_PATTERNS`) because a bare 500 from arbitrary endpoints is\n * too broad to retry blindly; it is only safe to treat as transient for the\n * compare endpoint, alongside the explicit \"not_available\" / \"heavy server\n * load\" markers.\n */\nconst TRANSIENT_COMPARE_API_PATTERNS = ['this diff is temporarily unavailable', 'temporarily unavailable due to heavy server load', 'heavy server load', 'not_available', 'http 500', 'http 502', 'http 503', 'http 504'];\n\n/**\n * Detect whether `error` represents a transient failure of GitHub's\n * compare/diff endpoint (issue #1829). Returns true for the documented\n * \"heavy server load\" / `not_available` HTTP 500 response as well as the\n * standard transient gateway codes (502/503/504), so the auto-PR readiness\n * gate can fall through to PR creation rather than aborting.\n *\n * @param {unknown} error\n * @returns {boolean}\n */\nconst isTransientCompareApiError = error => {\n  const text = collectErrorText(error).toLowerCase();\n  if (!text) return false;\n  return TRANSIENT_COMPARE_API_PATTERNS.some(pattern => text.includes(pattern));\n};\n\n/**\n * Wrap `fn` so that GitHub rate-limit errors are converted into a sleep until\n * (resetTime + bufferMs + jitterMs) followed by a retry. Other errors are rethrown immediately so we\n * don't mask programming bugs or 404s.\n *\n * Issue #1726 — rate-limit retry. Waiting ${waitMinutes} min (${resetSummary}; buffer ${Math.round(bufferMs / 60_000)} min + jitter ${Math.round(jitterMs / 1000)}s) until ${deadline.toISOString()}.`));\n        await sleepWithCountdown(waitMs, log);\n        continue;\n      }\n\n      if (isTransientNetworkError(error)) {\n        transientAttempts++;\n        if (transientAttempts >= transientMaxAttempts) {\n          await Promise.resolve(log(`❌ ${label}: transient network error persisted after ${transientAttempts} attempts; giving up.`));\n          throw error;\n        }\n        const waitMs = transientDelay * Math.pow(transientBackoff, transientAttempts - 1);\n        await Promise.resolve(log(`⚠️ ${label}: transient network error (attempt ${transientAttempts}/${transientMaxAttempts}), retrying in ${Math.round(waitMs / 1000)}s...`));\n        await sleepWithCountdown(waitMs, log);\n        continue;\n      }\n\n      throw error;\n    }\n  }\n  // Unreachable — loop either returns or throws via the budgets above.\n  throw lastError;\n};\n\n/**\n * Convenience wrapper around child_process.exec that retries on rate-limit\n * errors. Bare `${value}` interpolation is shell-escaped correctly; wrapping a placeholder in quotes (`\"${value}\"`) leaks literal quotes — that was issue #2119.\n   - **`capture: true` is mandatory alongside `mirror: false`** — dropping it would silence the probe *and* its caller's answer.\n   - **Injected-`\n\n hazard**: many helpers take `\n\n as a function parameter; test doubles are plain tagged templates `(strings, ...values) => …` that throw `TypeError: strings.reduce is not a function` on `$({...})`. Hence the defensive `quietProbe($)` helper for injected-`\n\n sites vs. direct `$(QUIET_PROBE)` for module-owned `\n\n.\n   - **Formal AI direct-endpoint architecture (prior sessions)**: `formal-ai serve --agent-mode` with `cwd` = repo clone + `HOME=<isolated> formal-ai with --global --no-start-server --base-url <url> <tool>` to materialise config, then native CLI invocation with the resulting env. Full content:\n     ```js\n     #!/usr/bin/env node\n     /**\n      * Read-only probes that must not be mirrored into the attached log.\n      *\n      * Issue #2130 — the solver mirrors every child process's output to stdout, and\n      * `src/lib.mjs` copies stdout into the log file that is later attached to the\n      * pull request. That is the right default for the AI tool's own output, but it\n      * also dumped the raw answers of the solver's internal probes between its own\n      * sentences, where they read as unexplained output or as errors:\n      *\n      *   - `gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/pulls/N` — a ~33 KB JSON object, once per watch\n      *     iteration (12 copies in the log captured for this issue);\n      *   - `gh api .../comments --paginate` — up to 46 KB per restart;\n      *   - `gh auth status --show-token` — a live credential in clear text;\n      *   - bare one-word answers such as a login, `public`, `I_kwDO...`, or a commit\n      *     SHA, with nothing around them to say what asked the question.\n      *\n      * Every one of those call sites already reports what it learned in words, so\n      * the raw output is captured for the caller but never mirrored.\n      *\n      * @module quiet-probe\n      */\n\n     /**\n      * command-stream options for a probe whose raw output stays out of the log.\n      * `capture: true` keeps `result.stdout` available to the caller.\n      *\n      *   const result = await $(QUIET_PROBE)`gh api user --jq .login`;\n      */\n     export const QUIET_PROBE = Object.freeze({ mirror: false, capture: true });\n\n     const quietProbeCache = new WeakMap();\n\n     /**\n      * Bind {@link QUIET_PROBE} to a `\n\n that arrived as a function argument,\n      * degrading to the tag itself when that `\n\n does not implement command-stream's\n      * options-call form.\n      *\n      * Many helpers take `\n\n as an injected parameter, and the doubles supplied by\n      * callers (tests, in particular) are plain tagged templates that throw on\n      * `$({ ... })`. Suppressing mirrored output is a readability improvement, never\n      * a correctness requirement, so a `\n\n that cannot be configured is used as-is\n      * rather than turned into a crash.\n      *\n      *   const result = await quietProbe($)`gh api user --jq .login`;\n      *\n      * @param {Function} dollar - a command-stream `\n\n or a tagged-template double.\n      * @returns {Function} `dollar` bound to the quiet options, or `dollar` itself.\n      */\n     export const quietProbe = dollar => {\n       if (typeof dollar !== 'function') return dollar;\n       const cached = quietProbeCache.get(dollar);\n       if (cached) return cached;\n       let bound = dollar;\n       try {\n         const candidate = dollar(QUIET_PROBE);\n         // A tag that ignores the options call may return a promise for a command it\n         // never should have run; swallow it so it cannot surface as an unhandled\n         // rejection, and keep the original tag.\n         if (typeof candidate?.catch === 'function') candidate.catch(() => {});\n         if (typeof candidate === 'function') bound = candidate;\n       } catch {\n         /* not option-callable - use the tag unchanged */\n       }\n       quietProbeCache.set(dollar, bound);\n       return bound;\n     };\n\n     export default {\n       QUIET_PROBE,\n       quietProbe,\n     };\n     ```\n\n   - **`src/github-rate-limit.lib.mjs`** — MODIFIED (uncommitted). `wrapDollarWithGhRetry` now forwards command-stream's options-call form so `$({ mirror: false, capture: true })` composes with rate-limit retry (all 24 modules build `\n\n via this wrapper). aky-timeout-test\nissue-865-agent-default-model\nissue-867-agent-error-not-treated-as-error\nissue-871-pricing-estimation\nissue-873-phantom-error-detection\nissue-878-docker-pr-check-optimization\nissue-879-helm-release-ci-failure\nissue-882-tool-agent-infinite-loop\nissue-884-workflow-syntax-error\nissue-886\nissue-886-false-positive-error-detection\nissue-890-session-id-extraction.md\nissue-894-missing-final-log-link\nissue-895-agent-infinite-restart-loop\nissue-906\nissue-912\nissue-916\nissue-923\nissue-94\nissue-940\nissue-942\nissue-944\nissue-946\nissue-952\nissue-954\nissue-958\nissue-962\nissue-964\nissue-967\nissue-969\nissue-971\nissue-972\nissue-975\nissue-982\nissue-984-harmful-prompts\nissue-986\nissue-989\nissue-991\nissue-995\nissue-998\npdf-failure-issue-655\nphp-installation-analysis.md\npr-4-ci-log-issue\npr-4-revert-issue\npr-52-log.txt\npr-609-comment-handling\nsolution-draft-log-pr-864.txt\n=== sample ===\nREADME.md\nanalysis.md\ndata\n# Case Study: Telegram Bot Token Leak via Bash Tool Comment (#1745)\n\n## Overview\n\nThe Telegram bot token (`8490528355:AAGHe...ItHCY`, **now revoked**) was published in\nplain text inside a public-facing pull-request comment authored by the AI agent\nrunning under our `solve.mjs`/interactive-mode bridge.\n\nThe leak surface: the agent ran `env` (or a process-environment dump command)\ninside a `Bash` tool call, and `interactive-mode.lib.mjs` posted the **raw**\noutput of that tool back into the PR as a comment without running it through\n`sanitizeLogContent`.\n\n**Source data:**\n\n- Leaked PR comment: `xlab2016/space_db_private/pull/20#issuecomment-4104547747`\n  ([raw JSON](data/leaked-comment.txt))\n- Original bug report: [issue #1745](data/issue-1745.json)\n- Existing token sanitizer: [`src/token-sanitization.lib.mjs`](../../../src/token-sanitization.lib.mjs)\n- Existing case study covering the same comment surface: [issue-1458 analysis](../issue-1458/analysis.md)\n\n---\n\n## Timeline of Events\n\n| Time (UTC)          | Event                                                                                                                                                                            |\n| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| 2026-03-21 21:54:53 | `xlab2016/space_db_private/pull/20` interactive Claude session starts (system.init)                                                                                              |\n| 2026-03-21 21:59:24 | Agent issues a `Bash` tool call whose output includes the process environment block (env vars including `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=[REDACTED]     |\n| 2026-03-21 21:59:25 | `interactive-mode.lib.mjs#handleToolResult` edits the matching tool-use comment with the raw bash output verbatim — **no sanitization applied** — token now public on github.com |\n| 2026-05-02 14:27    | Issue #1745 filed; token revoked in @BotFather                                                                                                                                   |\n\n---\n\n## Root Cause\n\n`interactive-mode.lib.mjs` exposes two posting helpers, `postComment` and\n`editComment`, that each call `gh api ... -X POST/PATCH --input -` with a JSON\nbody assembled from raw event data. The Bash-tool result handler embeds the\noutput into a fenced `bash` code block via:\n\n````js\nconst truncatedContent = truncateMiddle(content, { maxLines: 60, keepStart: 25, keepEnd: 25 });\nconst mergedComment = `## ${toolIcon} ${toolName} tool use\n\n${inputDisplay}\n\n${createCollapsible(`📤 Output (${statusIcon} ${statusText.toLowerCase()})`, '```\\n' + escapeMarkdown(truncatedContent) + '\\n```', true)}\n...`;\n````\n\n`truncatedContent` is the **untouched stdout/stderr** of the Bash tool. When\nthe agent runs `env`, `set`, `printenv`, `cat .env`, or any command that\nincludes secret-bearing strings in its stdout, those strings flow straight\nthrough `escapeMarkdown` (which doesn't redact secrets) and into the comment.\n\n`token-sanitization.lib.mjs` already exists and is invoked from\n`github.lib.mjs` for **log uploads** (gist + attached log file). It is **not**\ncalled from `interactive-mode.lib.mjs` — the inline tool-use comments bypass\nit entirely. That is the gap.",

  }
